name: Soliton reflector (natural)
description: A glider reflector built only from the medium's own structures: a chain of five still solitons. In this medium (k = 0.065, otherwise moreLifelike) a lone soliton neither moves nor divides, and gliders still run. Each glider in the train meets the chain at a shallow angle and turns about 90°, leaving the chain intact. Successive gliders exit on slightly different lanes because each one's history trail (c) nudges the next. Solitons also eat gliders that hit them dead-centre, and a glider that clips one at offset 8–12 knocks it loose, releasing a second glider. Nothing is painted: a second row of solitons 14 px apart below the reflector eats the outgoing gliders (a soliton absorbs a glider that hits it within about 6 px of centre), so they don't wrap round the torus. The catch nudges a couple of solitons a few pixels.
